_comment: Golden fixtures for M3's LOCAL verbs — camera, panels and LOS-honest queries (PLAN-metalstorm-command-language.md §6.2-§6.4). Every fixture here sets `ports: true`, so it runs against the REAL CameraPort (over a recording worker channel), the REAL UiActionRegistry and the REAL QueryEngine. The M1 fixtures in groups-ui-query.json keep running the same kinds with NO ports, which is still a live configuration and still has to refuse by name — the two files cover the two states.
_los: The LOS-honesty fixtures are the point of this file. A context makes an enemy exist OUT of LOS by leaving it out of `visible` — there is no visible:false flag, because the real mirror has no such thing. `enemy-out-of-los` and `enemy-in-los` differ ONLY in that one list, so the pair proves the answer tracks vision rather than the question.

fixtures.name: zoom to a region moves the camera there
zoom to a grid sector — the M2 sector names, addressed by camera
a camera target that resolves to nothing refuses — it does not frame the origin
fixtures.note: The failure mode this replaced: the M1 port signature returned void, so the executor printed 'camera on Atlantis' for a name nothing resolved. A port that can fail has to be able to say so.

saysLike: I don't know a place or force called "Atlantis"

fixtures.name: an ambiguous camera target still asks
fixtures.note: Camera resolution is non-strict (score dominance is enough — framing the wrong hill costs a keystroke, not the line), but a genuine tie is still a question. 'Rand' ties at the prefix tier.

fixtures.name: the whole map
zoom in scales the CURRENT distance
fixtures.note: The worker exposes an absolute orbit distance, not a step, so the port reads the live pose and scales it. The fixture pose sits ~1131 elmos out; one step in is 0.6× that.

fixtures.name: follow a squad tracks its centroid
fixtures.note: The first frame is immediate — a follow that waited a tick before moving would look broken. Chimera's eight members are spread around (900, 1100).

saysLike: move the camera yourself to stop

fixtures.name: following a place says so instead of pretending to follow it
fixtures.note: A region doesn't move. Saying 'following' would be a small lie that makes the camera look broken when it never moves again.

fixtures.name: following a squad with nothing in the mirror refuses
fixtures.note: No snapshot ⇒ no centroid ⇒ nothing to follow. Starting a follow that never moves the camera is indistinguishable from a broken one.

fixtures.name: the minimap goes full screen
fixtures.utterance: show me the minimap, full screen
fixtures.note: A plan §0 example utterance, and the one registry entry that HAS a full-screen mode. It changes the canvas size and nothing else — same scene, same ortho frustum, same team fog.

fixtures.name: "full screen" on a panel that has no such mode refuses by name
fixtures.utterance: show me the scoreboard full screen
fixtures.note: Falling back to `open` would give the player a 236px rail panel for a sentence that asked for the opposite — the kind of lie that makes a voice interface feel broken.

fixtures.name: the diplomacy panel opens by alias
fixtures.note: `parley-panel` is what the manifest calls it and 'diplomacy panel' is what a player says. The alias lives in metalstorm.ui.json next to the title, not in a client-side table that would drift from it.

fixtures.name: closing a panel reports it closed
a panel nobody registered refuses instead of opening the nearest one
fixtures.note: There is no fuzzy fallback in the registry. Opening the closest-sounding panel to a word the player didn't say is worse than admitting the miss.

fixtures.name: how many tanks — counted from the mirror, joined on ms_class
fixtures.utterance: how many tanks do we have
fixtures.note: 19 tank-class units: Chimera 8 + Basilisk 6 + Warhound 5 (its two attached engineers are engineers, so they are NOT counted — a squad's dominant class picks the SQUAD, but a count counts units).

fixtures.name: how many HEAVY tanks — the scale narrows it
fixtures.utterance: how many heavy tanks do we have left?
fixtures.note: A plan §0 example utterance. Chimera (8) + Basilisk (6) are ms_scale 3; Warhound is scale 2 and drops out.

fixtures.name: a class you own none of answers zero, not an error
fixtures.utterance: how many ships do we have

fixtures.name: an enemy count is qualified by what is spotted
fixtures.utterance: how many enemy tanks are there
fixtures.note: "3 enemy tanks in sight" is true; "the enemy has 3 tanks" would be a guess dressed as a fact. The wording carries the difference.

fixtures.name: LOS-HONESTY — an enemy that exists outside LOS is "not currently spotted"
fixtures.note: THE pillar-3 fixture. The board HAS enemy tanks — `enemy-out-of-los` documents them — but they are not in `visible`, i.e. not in the player's filtered stream. The engine cannot see them because there is nothing unfiltered for it to read, and it must say 'not currently spotted' rather than 'you have none' or nothing at all. The camera must not move either: a camera that swung to an unspotted enemy would be the wallhack the words denied.

fixtures.name: LOS-HONESTY, the other half — spotted enemies get a position
fixtures.note: Identical utterance, identical board except that the enemy tanks ARE in `visible`. If this one didn't answer with a place, the fixture above would be passing for the wrong reason (a query engine that never finds anything).

fixtures.name: where is my own squad — from the same mirror, with a region name
locating a place points the camera at it
fixtures.note: A place name is public knowledge — it arrived on the same rulesParams stream every client gets — so framing one reveals nothing that wasn't already shared.

fixtures.name: locating something that is neither a place nor a unit class refuses
fixtures.note: 'commander' is not in the shipped class vocabulary and no enemy-force producer exists yet, so there is nothing to resolve. The name refusal is the useful one — a vaguer 'I can't answer that' would hide which half failed.

saysLike: don't know a place or force

fixtures.name: no census means no answer — never an answer of zero
fixtures.utterance: how many tanks do we have
fixtures.note: "You have no tanks" and "I can't see your units right now" are different claims and only one of them is true here. This is the assertion that keeps them apart.

saysLike: can't read your units right now

fixtures.name: authority, from the team rules params
fixtures.utterance: how much authority do we have

fixtures.name: objectives lists only the active ones
fixtures.utterance: what are we supposed to be doing
fixtures.note: A settled objective is not the answer to 'what now'. Objective 2 is complete and must not appear.

fixtures.name: asking is never ordering, even in a multi-action envelope
fixtures.utterance: zoom to Northgate and tell me how many tanks we have
fixtures.note: The one rule that has to hold across every kind in this file: nothing here reaches sendCommand. A camera move and a question are not orders and cost no authority.
